clue.text: Act in earth to produce superior fuel

indicators.note: the letters of the first three words are reworked to produce a new word

explanation.surface: Some performance in the ground yields a top-grade fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to produce' signals rearranging ACT IN EARTH into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthracite is the hardest, highest-grade coal, burning hot with little smoke.

clue.text: Symbol of eternal life held by Tutankhamen

indicators.note: the answer is held within the letters of the pharaoh's name

explanation.surface: An Egyptian life-symbol clutched by the boy king Tutankhamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' points to the run of letters tucked inside 'Tutankhamen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankh is the looped cross of ancient Egypt standing for eternal life.

clue.text: Defensible bleat, perhaps, about England's openers

indicators.note: the rearranged bleat goes about, i.e. around, the other piece
perhaps suggests the letters of bleat could be arranged some other way

parts.note: the opening two letters of England are E and N

explanation.surface: A sheep's cry made in defence, wrapped round the start of an English innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the bleat into TABLE, and 'about' wraps it round the opening pair of 'England', splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A position that is tenable can be held or defended against attack.

clue.text: Corrupted son, I make facsimiles of works of art

indicators.note: the letters of the first three words are used to make a new word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dishonest son confesses to forging copies of paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' signals reworking CORRUPTED SON I into the answer; 'Corrupted' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Reproductions are copies made of original paintings or sculptures.

clue.text: Country producing a tin a day, almost

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: almost means the word day loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A nation whose output is one tin each day, or nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from 'day', leaving DA.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a nation in North America.

clue.text: In the future there will be a cat-fight about men

indicators.note: the cat-fight pieces go about, i.e. around, the men

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a row is a quarrel or fight
OR, other ranks, are the ordinary soldiers or men in the army

explanation.surface: A prophecy that one day a catfight will break out over some men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts OR inside TOM + ROW. OR (other ranks) is the crossword convention for enlisted men, as opposed to officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomorrow is used loosely for the time ahead, the days to come.

clue.text: Greyish-yellow colour for city rugby

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
RU stands for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A dull shade chosen as the kit colour for a city rugby team.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postal district covering the City, London's financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is the pale beige shade of unbleached linen.

clue.text: Get up, we hear, livery

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Get up, we hear, livery (7)' for COSTUME: 'Get up' defines it, but no word for livery sounds like the answer, so the homophone piece cannot be parsed; likely OCR damage or a lost word.

clue.text: Firm not producing

definitions.meaning: firm means steadfast, not giving way
producing nothing, giving no yield or crop

explanation.definitionFit: Unyielding is resolute and inflexible; read as un-yielding, it means bearing no return.

clue.text: Principal peg for a bowler to aim at?

definitions.meaning: principal as a noun is the chief person in an organisation

definitions.text: peg for a bowler to aim at
definitions.meaning: in skittles or bowling the central pin is the one to knock down

explanation.surface: The main target pin for someone bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingpin is both the most important figure and the large central skittle.

clue.text: Grandeur of Sally in springtime

indicators.note: in places the sally inside the month

parts.note: May is a month of spring
a sally is a witty remark, a jest

explanation.surface: The splendour of a girl named Sally in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a girl's name, but here it is a witty remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is regal dignity and impressive splendour.

clue.text: Kipling's meticulous accounts published

parts.note: just so means exactly right, precise
stories are accounts or narratives

explanation.surface: Rudyard Kipling's careful records go to print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kipling's' stands for his famous book of animal tales; 'published' is a link pointing to a book title.
explanation.definitionFit: This collection of children's fables explaining how animals got their features was written by Rudyard Kipling.

clue.text: Family stress? Doctors take it in examinations

parts.note: blood means kin or family
pressure means stress or strain

explanation.surface: Family tension worries the doctors during check-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a reading that GPs routinely take during check-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicians measure the force of circulation in the arteries with a cuff at check-ups.

clue.text: Bread wrappers?

parts.note: bread is slang for money, so these are the envelopes in which wages were handed out

explanation.definitionFit: Wage envelopes literally wrap 'bread', slang for cash.

clue.text: Boulevard, a meeting-place

parts.note: a venue is a place where people meet

explanation.surface: A broad street serving as a place to gather.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a wide, often tree-lined, street, like a boulevard.

clue.text: Unsettled detail in slack terminal

parts.note: slack means loose, not tight
a terminal is an end point

explanation.surface: An outstanding detail lingers in a quiet airport terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose end is a matter left unresolved.

clue.text: Spider at spinning, having trudged wearily

indicators.note: spinning suggests the letters of spider at are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: A spider spinning its web has worn itself out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' fits a spider's work, but it signals rearranging SPIDER AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or reluctantly, plodding along.

clue.text: Helpful pieces of information from gun dogs

definitions.meaning: tips or hints that guide someone
hunting dogs that freeze to indicate where game lies

explanation.surface: Getting useful tips from hunting dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointers are tips, and also a breed of hunting dog that stands still to indicate game.

clue.text: Popular ways to make attacks

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
roads are ways

explanation.surface: Well-used routes for launching raids.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are raids or incursions into hostile territory.

clue.text: A southern sea-bird with the rear first?

parts.note: a tern is a sea-bird

explanation.surface: A gull from the south flying backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on moving backwards, stern first, which is what astern means for a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means at or towards the back of a ship, or moving backwards.

clue.text: Points above net? Catch!

indicators.note: in a down clue the points sit above the net, so they come first

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
a snare is a net or trap

explanation.surface: In tennis, points won at the net, followed by a shout to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to trap or capture something.

clue.text: Writer's "to be or not to be" say?

definitions.text: Writer's "to be or not to be" say?

parts.words: Writer's "to be or not to be" say
parts.note: a writing tool whose marks can be rubbed out, so whatever it writes may stay or may not

explanation.definitionFit: Pencil marks are provisional, as when something is pencilled in, so they may or may not last.

clue.text: Scour a bonfire put out and yielding charcoal

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters of the first three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cleaning up after a bonfire is extinguished leaves charred remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' fits a bonfire, but it signals rearranging SCOUR A BONFIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carboniferous means bearing carbon or coal, the geological age that laid down coal seams.

clue.text: County no longer known

definitions.meaning: an English shire in the south-east
an archaic word for known, past participle of ken

explanation.definitionFit: Kent is a county in south-east England; kent is an obsolete Scots form meaning known.

clue.text: Ecstasy runs out as energy declines

annotationWithheld.clue: Ecstasy runs out as energy declines

clue.text: Word newly-invented for company in later life

parts.note: age means old age, later life

explanation.surface: A newly made-up word for a business in its twilight years.
explanation.definitionFit: A coinage is a freshly minted word or phrase.

clue.text: Son has broken window-frame

indicators.note: broken means the letters of has are shattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy has smashed the window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' makes ASH from the three letters of 'has'; 'window-frame' is the definition, not part of the breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the sliding frame holding the glass in a sash window.

clue.text: Teenager with an allowance — transported, we hear

parts.note: dole is a benefit payment, an allowance

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for transported is sounded rather than spelt

parts.note: sent means transported, carried away in ecstasy

explanation.surface: A youngster with pocket money is thrilled, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns SENT into SCENT. The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a young person between childhood and adulthood.
